clinical_category: Alendronate - safe oral administration and esophageal injury prevention
blueprint_topic: Medication administration teaching and prevention of adverse effects
stem: A client is prescribed oral alendronate for osteoporosis. Which statement by the client indicates correct understanding of administration?

options.A: I will take it after getting up with 6 to 8 ounces of plain water, before my first food or other medication, and I will remain upright for at least 30 minutes and until after I eat.
options.B: I will take it at bedtime with a small sip of water so the medication remains in contact with my esophagus overnight.
options.C: I will take it with breakfast and milk because food and calcium improve alendronate absorption and protect the esophagus.
options.D: I can lie down immediately after swallowing it as long as I took the tablet with water.

rationale: A is correct. Current alendronate labeling directs patients to take the tablet upon arising with 6 to 8 ounces of plain water, at least 30 minutes before the first food, beverage, or medication of the day, and not to lie down for at least 30 minutes and until after the first food of the day. These instructions facilitate delivery to the stomach, reduce the potential for esophageal irritation, and avoid reduced absorption from food, beverages, or other medications. B and D increase the risk of prolonged esophageal contact and contradict the upright-position instructions. C is incorrect because food and beverages other than plain water, including calcium-containing products, can reduce absorption. The final item tests the complete label-supported administration sequence rather than asking only for the name of the complication.
educational_objective: Administer oral alendronate safely by taking it on arising with plain water before food or other medications and remaining upright for at least 30 minutes and until after the first meal to reduce esophageal irritation and preserve absorption.
source_organization: DailyMed, U.S. National Library of Medicine
source_document_title: ALENDRONATE SODIUM tablet — Full Prescribing Information
source_version_date: DailyMed updated 2026-05-21; recent major labeling change 2026-02
source_locator: Section 2.6 Important Administration Instructions: take upon arising with 6-8 ounces plain water at least 30 minutes before first food, beverage or medication; do not lie down for at least 30 minutes and until after first food; instructions facilitate delivery to stomach, reduce esophageal irritation and preserve absorption. Section 4 Contraindications: inability to stand/sit upright for at least 30 minutes and esophageal abnormalities delaying emptying. Section 5.1 Upper Gastrointestinal Adverse Reactions: oral alendronate can cause local upper-GI/esophageal irritation and dosing instructions must be followed.
source_claim_supported: The current DailyMed label directly supports the complete administration sequence, the 30-minute upright interval, plain-water requirement, food/medication separation, absorption effect, and rationale of reducing esophageal irritation.

correction_summary: Retained the correct esophageal-safety construct but replaced the generic FDA directory with a current May 2026 DailyMed label and rebuilt the item into complete administration teaching. Every numeric and administration detail in the correct answer is directly label-supported, and distractors now test realistic errors involving bedtime dosing, food/calcium coadministration and premature recumbency.
audit_findings: The original core rationale was correct but the item tested only the complication name and cited a generic FDA label directory.
Fresh DailyMed review verified a current label updated 2026-05-21 and directly supports every administration detail retained in the final answer.
The final item integrates absorption and esophageal-safety teaching without adding any unsupported interval, dose, or universal duration-of-therapy claim.
Distractors test bedtime recumbency, calcium/food coadministration and immediate lying down; none is defensible under the label.
